data.reason: WAN NIC vtnet0 transmit path is hung: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flaps, netstat shows 48211 output packets dropped due to no bufs / Oerrs on vtnet0, pings fail with ENOBUFS, and ARP for the ISP next hop 198.51.100.1 is (incomplete). The cable modem already self-rebooted at 02:28 and reports OPERATIONAL with good SNR, so the provider side is fine; 12 WAN DHCP reloads did not clear the stuck NIC. Only a full firewall reboot resets the hung driver/NIC state.

data.component: WAN NIC/driver (vtnet0) transmit hang on the firewall
data.cause: The firewall's WAN NIC/driver (vtnet0) entered a stuck transmit state (repeated queue-0 watchdog timeouts and link flaps, output drops for no buffers), so traffic cannot reach the ISP even though the DHCP lease is valid and the provider/modem side is healthy.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' with link DOWN/UP flaps on the WAN NIC
netstat -s reports '48211 output packets dropped due to no bufs, etc.' and netstat -i shows Oerrs=48211 on vtnet0
ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 (ISP next hop) fails with 'sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss
arp -a shows the gateway 198.51.100.1 as '(incomplete)' while the WAN IP 198.51.100.27 is still configured (ifconfig -a)
/var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 shows a valid lease (renew 2026/3/5), so the outage is not an expired DHCP lease
/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl shows 12 reloads in 24h all rc=0 yet down_seconds=5040, ending in 'reload_cap' at 03:30 — WAN reloads did not restore connectivity
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl show the cable modem self-rebooted at 02:28 and reports OPERATIONAL with good SNR (~37.7 dB), so the provider side is fine
data.recommendation: Reboot gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 transmit path. WAN DHCP reloads (wan_reload) already ran repeatedly with rc=0 without restoring traffic, so only a full reboot clears the stuck NIC/driver state; I requested firewall_reboot, which the harness applied as a drill since the maintainer was unreachable. After boot, verify ping to 198.51.100.1 succeeds and ARP for the gateway resolves. If the watchdog timeouts recur on this NIC, inspect or replace the (virtualized) WAN NIC / its hypervisor backing.
